title: GitSpawn flaw lets some coding agents execute repository-controlled commands
friendlyTitle: A project folder can attack some AI coding tools before work begins
summary: Manifold Security found that several coding agents ran Git context commands without neutralizing executable settings in a repository's local Git configuration. A project delivered with its .git directory intact could therefore run code as the user; some affected products were patched, while the researchers reported four findings still unpatched at publication.
friendlySummary: Some coding agents automatically ask Git about a project. A specially prepared project folder can use that step to run a hidden command on the user's computer.
whyItMatters: Do not open an untrusted project archive or synced folder directly in a coding agent. Clone from a trusted remote when possible, inspect .git/config before use, keep agents updated and isolate unfamiliar repositories from valuable credentials and files.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Treat downloaded project folders as untrusted. Check them first, update your coding tool and keep important keys away from test environments.
